records.source: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν ζωῆς τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Τιμοθέῳ ἀγαπητῷ τέκνῳ· χάρις, ἔλεος, εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God according to [the] promise of life the [one] in Christ Jesus, \v 2 to Timothy beloved child: grace, mercy, peace from God Father and Christ Jesus the Lord of us.
pieces: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, sent to proclaim the promise of life that is in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus,
to Timothy, my dear son. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God the Father and from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

L.1: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, in keeping with the promise of life that is in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus,
L.2: to Timothy, [my] beloved child: grace, mercy, peace from God [the] Father and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

R.1: This letter is from Paul. God chose me to be an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, to tell people about the life God has promised, the life we have when we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
R.2: I am writing to Timothy, who is like a dear son to me. I pray that God the Father and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord will show you grace and mercy and give you peace.

decisions.choice: according to the promise of life: an apostle for the sake of the promised life
alternatives: an apostle as the promise of life planned
decisions.reason: κατ may give the purpose of Paul's apostleship (to make known the promise of life) or its standard. The life is eternal life, found in Christ (verse 10).

decisions.choice: Timothy, beloved child: Paul's last letter to him
decisions.reason: The letter is written from prison in Rome (1:8, 1:17), near the end of Paul's life (4:6-8). As with 1 Timothy, its authorship has been questioned since the nineteenth century; it presents itself as Paul's.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: sent to proclaim the promise of life (B); to tell people about the life God has promised (R)
alternatives: according to the promise of life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m1.

decisions.choice: son
decisions.reason: The picture is of a father and son, as in 1 Timothy 1:2.

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ θεῷ, ᾧ λατρεύω ἀπὸ προγόνων ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὡς ἀδιάλειπτον ἔχω τὴν περὶ σοῦ μνείαν ἐν ταῖς δεήσεσίν μου, νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐπιποθῶν σε ἰδεῖν, μεμνημένος σου τῶν δακρύων, ἵνα χαρᾶς πληρωθῶ ὑπόμνησιν λαβὼν τῆς ἐν σοὶ ἀνυποκρίτου πίστεως, ἥτις ἐνῴκησεν πρῶτον ἐν τῇ μάμμῃ σου Λωΐδι καὶ τῇ μητρί σου Εὐνίκῃ, πέπεισμαι δὲ ὅτι καὶ ἐν σοί.
records.gloss: Thanks I have to the God, whom I serve from forefathers with a clean conscience, as unceasing I have the concerning you remembrance in the prayers of me night and day, \v 4 longing you to see, remembering your tears, so that with joy I may be filled, \v 5 reminder having received of the in you sincere faith, which dwelt first in the grandmother of you Lois and the mother of you Eunice, I am persuaded but that also in you.
pieces: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my ancestors did, whenever I remember you in my prayers, as I do night and day.
I remember your tears, and I long to see you, so that my joy may be complete.
I recall your sincere faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and which I am sure now lives in you.

L.3: I give thanks to God, whom I serve as [my] forefathers did with a clear conscience, as I remember you constantly in my prayers night and day,
L.4: longing to see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
L.5: being reminded of the sincere faith in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded [it lives] in you as well.

R.3: I serve God, as my ancestors did, and my conscience is clear. I thank God for you when I pray for you, and I pray for you all the time, day and night.
R.4: I remember how you cried when we said goodbye, and I want very much to see you. That would fill me with joy.
R.5: I remember your faith, which is real. Your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice had this faith first, and I am sure that you have it now too.

decisions.choice: I give thanks
decisions.reason: Χάριν is the word for grace, but in this phrase it means thanks (1 Timothy 1:12).

decisions.choice: as my forefathers did: Paul's worship continues that of his Jewish ancestors
decisions.reason: Paul served the God of Israel as his ancestors had (Acts 24:14; Philippians 3:5).

decisions.choice: your tears: perhaps at their parting
decisions.reason: The letter does not say when; compare the tears at Paul's parting from the Ephesian elders (Acts 20:37-38).

decisions.choice: Lois and Eunice: Timothy's grandmother and mother
decisions.reason: Acts 16:1 says Timothy's mother was a Jewish believer and his father a Greek. Timothy knew the Scriptures from childhood (3:15).

decisions.choice: give thanks (L); thank (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sense is thanks (m1), so the key term "grace" is not used for this word.

decisions.choice: how you cried when we said goodbye
decisions.reason: Readable states a likely occasion (m3).

records.heading: Thanks for Timothy's sincere faith

records.source: δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἀναμιμνῄσκω σε ἀναζωπυρεῖν τὸ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν σοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν μου·
records.gloss: For which reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of the God, which is in you through the laying on of the hands of me;
pieces: That is why I remind you to stir up into flame the gift God gave you when I laid my hands on you.

L.6: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.

R.6: So I want to remind you to keep using the gift God gave you when I put my hands on you. Let it burn brightly, like a fire.

decisions.choice: fan into flame: rekindle a fire
decisions.reason: ἀναζωπυρέω is to stir up the embers of a fire into a flame. The gift is not lost but needs to be used.

decisions.choice: the laying on of my hands
decisions.reason: Paul had laid hands on Timothy, with the elders (1 Timothy 4:14), setting him apart for his work.

decisions.choice: keep using; Let it burn brightly, like a fire
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα δειλίας, ἀλλὰ δυνάμεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ σωφρονισμοῦ.
records.gloss: not for gave us the God a spirit of cowardice, but of power and of love and of self-control.
pieces: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but a spirit of power and love and sound judgment.

L.7: For God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and love and self-control.

R.7: God did not give us a spirit that makes us afraid. The Spirit God gave us makes us strong and loving, and helps us control ourselves.

decisions.choice: a spirit: the Spirit God gives, who brings power, love and self-control
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα may mean a human disposition ("a spirit of fear") or God's Spirit, described by what he produces. Since God gives it, and the Spirit dwells in believers (verse 14), the Holy Spirit is probably meant.

decisions.choice: cowardice and self-control
decisions.reason: δειλίας is timidity, cowardice; σωφρονισμοῦ is a sound, disciplined mind.

decisions.choice: The Spirit God gave us
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m1.

records.source: Μὴ οὖν ἐπαισχυνθῇς τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν μηδὲ ἐμὲ τὸν δέσμιον αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ συγκακοπάθησον τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ, τοῦ σώσαντος ἡμᾶς καὶ καλέσαντος κλήσει ἁγίᾳ, οὐ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ἡμῶν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἰδίαν πρόθεσιν καὶ χάριν, τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων, φανερωθεῖσαν δὲ νῦν διὰ τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καταργήσαντος μὲν τὸν θάνατον φωτίσαντος δὲ ζωὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἰς ὃ ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κῆρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος καὶ διδάσκαλος.
records.gloss: Not therefore be ashamed of the testimony of the Lord of us nor me the prisoner of him, but share in suffering for the gospel according to [the] power of God, \v 9 of the [one] having saved us and having called with a calling holy, not according to the works of us but according to his own purpose and grace, the [one] having been given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal, \v 10 having been revealed but now through the appearing of the Savior of us Christ Jesus, having abolished death, having brought to light but life and immortality through the gospel, \v 11 for which was appointed I a herald and apostle and teacher.
pieces: So do not be ashamed to testify about our Lord, or ashamed of me, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prisoner. Instead, share with me in suffering for the gospel, relying on the power of God.

He saved us and called us to a holy life, not because of anything we had done but because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own purpose and grace. This grace was given us in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus before eternal ages began,
and now it has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He has destroyed death and has brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
For this gospel I was appointed a herald, an apostle and a teacher.

L.8: So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, nor of me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prisoner, but share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God,
L.9: who saved us and called [us] with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own purpose and grace, which was given to us in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus before eternal ages,
L.10: but has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel,
L.11: for which I was appointed a herald and apostle and teacher.

R.8: So do not be ashamed to tell people about our Lord. And do not be ashamed of me because I am in prison for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Instead, be ready to suffer with me for the good news. God will give you the power you need.
R.9: God saved us and called us to live holy lives. It was not because of the good things we had done. It was because God had planned it, and because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace. God gave us this grace through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus before the eternal ages began.
R.10: But now God has shown it to us, because our Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has come. Jesus destroyed death. Through the good news {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed us the way to life that never ends.
R.11: God chose me to tell this good news, to be an apostle and to teach.

decisions.choice: the testimony about our Lord
decisions.reason: μαρτύριον τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν most naturally means the witness borne to the Lord, the gospel Paul preaches, which some found shameful (Romans 1:16).

decisions.choice: his prisoner: in prison for Christ
decisions.reason: As in Philemon 1, Paul is a prisoner because of Christ and belongs to him.

decisions.choice: not by our works, but by his purpose and grace
decisions.reason: Salvation rests on God's own purpose and grace, not on human achievement (Ephesians 2:8-9; Titus 3:5).

decisions.choice: before eternal ages: before time began
decisions.reason: πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων is literally "before eternal times": before the ages of the world (Titus 1:2).

decisions.choice: the appearing: Christ's coming into the world
decisions.reason: ἐπιφανείας here means Christ's first coming, his life, death and resurrection; elsewhere it is his return (4:1, 4:8).

decisions.choice: abolished death, brought immortality to light
decisions.reason: καταργέω is to make powerless (1 Corinthians 15:26); ἀφθαρσίαν is incorruption, life that cannot decay.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: before eternal ages (L); before eternal ages began (B); before the eternal ages began (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "eternal" is kept (m4).

decisions.choice: life that never ends
decisions.reason: Readable explains "immortality" (m6).

records.heading: Not ashamed of the gospel

records.source: δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν καὶ ταῦτα πάσχω, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνομαι, οἶδα γὰρ ᾧ πεπίστευκα, καὶ πέπεισμαι ὅτι δυνατός ἐστιν τὴν παραθήκην μου φυλάξαι εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν.
records.gloss: For which reason also these things I suffer, but not I am ashamed, I know for whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that able he is the deposit of me to guard until that day.
pieces: That is why I am suffering as I am. But I am not ashamed, because I know the one I have believed, and I am convinced that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to guard what I have entrusted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} until that day.

L.12: For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to guard my deposit until that day.

R.12: That is why I am suffering. But I am not ashamed, because I know the one I believe in. I am sure that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can keep safe what I have given into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} care until the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes back.

decisions.choice: my deposit: what I have entrusted to him
alternatives: what he has entrusted to me (the gospel, as in verse 14)
decisions.reason: παραθήκην μου is literally "my deposit". It may be what Paul has entrusted to God, his life and work, or the gospel God entrusted to Paul, which is what "deposit" means in verse 14 and 1 Timothy 6:20. Here God is the one who guards it, which suits the first reading better.

decisions.choice: that day: the day of Christ's coming and judgment
decisions.reason: As in 1:18 and 4:8.

decisions.choice: what I have entrusted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (B); what I have given into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} care (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m1, which is uncertain.

records.source: ὑποτύπωσιν ἔχε ὑγιαινόντων λόγων ὧν παρ’ ἐμοῦ ἤκουσας ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
records.gloss: A pattern hold of healthy words, which from me you heard, in faith and love the [ones] in Christ Jesus;
pieces: Keep to the pattern of sound teaching you heard from me, with the faith and love that are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.13: Hold to the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.13: Follow the true teaching you heard from me. Keep it as your model. Live with the faith and love that come from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

decisions.choice: a pattern: a model or outline to follow
decisions.reason: ὑποτύπωσιν is a sketch or model (1 Timothy 1:16). Timothy is to hold to the shape of the teaching Paul gave.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.source: τὴν καλὴν παραθήκην φύλαξον διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος ἐν ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: The good deposit guard through [the] Spirit Holy the [one] dwelling in us.
pieces: Guard the good treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who lives in us.

L.14: Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.

R.14: Protect the good teaching that God has given you. The Holy Spirit who lives in us will help you.

decisions.choice: the good deposit: the gospel entrusted to Timothy
decisions.reason: As in 1 Timothy 6:20: the truth placed in his care.

records.source: Οἶδας τοῦτο ὅτι ἀπεστράφησάν με πάντες οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ὧν ἐστιν Φύγελος καὶ Ἑρμογένης.
records.gloss: You know this, that turned away from me all those in Asia, of whom is Phygelus and Hermogenes.
pieces: You know that everyone in the province of Asia has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.

L.15: You know this, that all those in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.

R.15: You know that all the believers in the province of Asia have turned away from me. Phygelus and Hermogenes are two of them.

decisions.choice: all in Asia: the believers there generally, not every one
decisions.reason: Asia was the Roman province around Ephesus. "All" is an overstatement of grief: Onesiphorus, from Ephesus, did not desert him (verses 16-18).

decisions.choice: Phygelus and Hermogenes
decisions.reason: Nothing more is known of them.

records.heading: Deserted by many, refreshed by Onesiphorus

records.source: δῴη ἔλεος ὁ κύριος τῷ Ὀνησιφόρου οἴκῳ, ὅτι πολλάκις με ἀνέψυξεν, καὶ τὴν ἅλυσίν μου οὐκ ἐπαισχύνθη·
records.gloss: May give mercy the Lord to the of Onesiphorus household, because often me he refreshed, and the chain of me not he was ashamed of;
pieces: May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed that I was in chains.

L.16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain.

R.16: I pray that the Lord will be kind to the family of Onesiphorus. He often helped me and cheered me up. He was not ashamed that I was in prison.

decisions.choice: the household of Onesiphorus
decisions.reason: Paul prays for his household here and greets it in 4:19. Some have inferred that Onesiphorus had died, but the letter does not say so; he may simply have been away from home.

decisions.choice: not ashamed of my chain
decisions.reason: ἅλυσίν is a chain, as in Acts 28:20. Visiting a prisoner in chains brought risk and shame.

records.source: ἀλλὰ γενόμενος ἐν Ῥώμῃ σπουδαίως ἐζήτησέν με καὶ εὗρεν δῴη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος εὑρεῖν ἔλεος παρὰ κυρίου ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ὅσα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ διηκόνησεν, βέλτιον σὺ γινώσκεις.
records.gloss: but having been in Rome eagerly he sought me and found; \v 18 may give to him the Lord to find mercy from [the] Lord in that day; and how much in Ephesus he served, better you know.
pieces: Instead, when he came to Rome, he searched hard for me until he found me.
May the Lord grant that he find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know very well all the ways he helped in Ephesus.

L.17: But when he was in Rome, he searched for me eagerly and found [me].
L.18: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know very well how much he served in Ephesus.

R.17: When he came to Rome, he looked everywhere for me until he found me.
R.18: I pray that the Lord will be kind to him on the day when the Lord judges everyone. You know how much he helped me in Ephesus.

decisions.choice: Rome: where Paul was imprisoned
decisions.reason: The letter places Paul in prison in Rome, where it was hard to find him.

decisions.choice: may the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord
decisions.reason: The repetition of "Lord" may refer to Christ and to God, or simply be a fixed form of prayer.

decisions.choice: how much he served in Ephesus
decisions.reason: διακονέω is to serve: he helped Paul, and probably the church, in Ephesus.
